Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-10-20 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 46 minutes (actual)
- Attendees: Samir, Maya, Carlos, Priya, Ethan

Summary: quick check-in, share recent INT8/FP8 numbers, decide next steps for repro and rollout playbook.

[00:00] Samir: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, we wanted to run through the latest numbers from the quant pilot and then lock down the playbook for rollout — hope that time still works?
[00:12] Carlos: yeah good, appreciate it. we had a couple of nights of runs, saw — saw some interesting variance on the long chat flows.
[00:18] Maya: hi, everyone. quick context: we ran INT8 conversion on the 7B variant and FP8 blend on the 13B, measured token/sec and p95 latency, and also ran the evaluation harness from the shared repo.
[00:29] Priya: quick clarification — when you say p95 is that per-token or per-response? we need per-response for SLA mapping.
[00:36] Maya: per-response, yes — sorry, shoulda been explicit. token/sec is for throughput.
[00:43] Ethan: and which infra were you using for that run? cloud or dedicated?
[00:48] Maya: these were on Redwood hosted GPUs, standard c-type nodes — not customer on-prem. that's important because we saw one flow that balloons with KV cache misses on long contexts.
[00:58] Carlos: yeah we noticed that with our simulator too. when we hit 3k+ tokens the latency jumps. may be related to how the kayv cache is being warm — the transcriber often says "kay-vee" but it's KV cache.
[01:13] Samir: exactly — two possibilities: either the quantized kernel is causing micro-ops that increase memory pressure at longer contexts or batching heuristics need adjustment.
[01:24] Maya: and also sometimes the FP8 path has slightly higher numeric stability so the KV hits are more predictable, INT8 can be noisier for some attention patterns.
[01:33] Priya: were you seeing quality regressions in addition to latency? some of our business flows are quality-sensitive.
[01:39] Maya: small SNR drop in a subset of prompts — measured A/B score ~0.92 vs baseline for INT8 on high-entity extraction prompts. FP8 was 0.98.
[01:50] Carlos: hmm that's concerning. extraction is core for us. what's the margin of error? like human-labeled tolerance?
[01:56] Priya: our tolerance is basically >0.95 for these extraction tasks, below that ops flags it.
[02:02] Samir: ok, so FP8 meets that threshold, INT8 is borderline. we should identify gating: when INT8 passes specific prompt cohorts, we can flip to INT8 for cost reasons, otherwise FP8.
[02:15] Ethan: can you quantify cost delta again? we need to model for our CFO.
[02:19] Samir: yes — rough numbers from the pilot: INT8 gives ~1.9x token cost reduction vs FP32, FP8 gives ~1.6x. but real-world depends on batching and cache hit rates. we'll share the per-endpoint spreadsheet.
[02:33] Maya: point of note: at 4k token evals INT8 p95 increased by 40% on our hosted run for that one flow; FP8 only increased by 12%.
[02:45] Carlos: do you think that's reproducible on our infra? we run a slightly different kernel setup and our memory bus is different.
[02:52] Maya: that's why we recommended a rerun on your infra with the same harness — to validate. some of the timings are kernel and PCIe dependent.
[03:01] Priya: what's the proposed fallback playbook if we see regressions post-rollout?
[03:06] Samir: short playbook idea: 1) Canary: route 5% traffic to quantized variant with blocking thresholds, 2) Monitoring: SNR checks + synthetic prompt golden set, 3) Auto-fallback: if SNR drop > 3% or p95 > SLA + 20% for 10m, switch to FP8 or FP32, 4) Rollback: manual rollback if sustained.
[03:25] Ethan: can that be automated in your console? we don't want constant manual ops.
[03:29] Maya: yes we can wire automatic routing policies: canary percentages, automatic fallbacks, and a degrade-to-FP8 route. the console exposes tracing and the rollback hook.
[03:38] Carlos: and would audit logs show which token sequences triggered fallback? we need that for debugging.
[03:43] Samir: yes, token-level tracing is available but note PII — traces are sampled and hashed unless you run Private with full audit retention.
[03:52] Priya: security question — if we go Private, how does KMS integrate with our HSM? is it supported?
[03:57] Samir: yes, Redwood Private supports customer KMS/HSM integrations. we'll attach the excerpts from our security guide.
[04:05] Maya: back to performance: we also saw variance depending on the prompt prefix length distribution. prefix caching helps a lot — when prefix is long and reused across requests, latency drops significantly.
[04:18] Carlos: in our live traffic prefixes are moderately repetitive so cache should help. may be the case that a small tweak to batching will unlock more gains.
[04:26] Maya: agreed — we'll test a slightly higher batch timeout for INT8 to see if it lowers p95 without blowing up cost.
[04:33] Priya: let's talk about measurement: SNR was computed how? automated scorer?
[04:38] Maya: we used the eval harness: token-level BLEU-ish, F1 for extraction and a human-annotated subset for subjective metrics. there are noisy labels so we recommended adding 10 more human-labeled samples from you.
[04:50] Carlos: on the human side we can do that, we'll pull a quick sample.
[04:54] Ethan: for the rerun, can you give a short checklist of what you're going to capture? I want Infra to prep.
[05:00] Maya: checklist: same docker image and runtime kernels, exact model artifacts (we provide checksums), full perf logs (p95/p50/p99, token/sec), kv-cache hit/miss rates, system metrics (GPU mem, PCIe bandwidth), and the raw request/response pairs for the 10 sample prompts.
[05:16] Carlos: that works. we'll stand up a node with similar GPU flavor.
[05:20] Samir: timeline-wise we propose: Samir shares cost model doc by Fri, Maya kicks off reruns on your infra next Tue/Wed, customer provides prompt set by Sun, then we reconvene next Tuesday for readout.
[05:33] Priya: agreed. also want to highlight we may prefer FP8 on some endpoints where quality is critical and INT8 on bulk low-sensitivity endpoints.
[05:42] Maya: exactly — per-endpoint policy is easy with routing. you can pin endpoint A to FP8 and endpoint B to INT8, or do blended fallback.
[05:50] Ethan: any blockers on our side? latency budget is tight for mobile calls.
[05:55] Maya: mobile budgets are tricky because of tail latency. caching and short-circuiting help but we should validate with mobile-like request patterns.
[06:05] Carlos: we'll add a mobile traffic pattern to the rerun.
[06:08] Samir: quick note on observability: we'll enable per-token cost breakdown in console so you can see exact cost per route.
[06:15] Priya: perfect. security doc please as well.

--- mid-call technical dive (Maya leads) ---

[06:30] Maya: diving deeper into the int8 instability we profiled kernel traces; the quantized matmul sometimes falls back to a micro-kernel that emits more memory traffic at long K/V lengths — that contributes to p95. in some cases a small reorder of operations helped.
[06:45] Carlos: is that something you can tune without retraining? any weight clipping or calibration?
[06:51] Maya: mostly calibration-level changes and per-layer clipping thresholds; no retraining required for these experiments. we can try a per-head scale adjustment that reduced noise on the extraction prompts.
[07:03] Priya: what's the risk of such calibration on other prompts? could it overfit?
[07:08] Maya: small risk. that's why we run the golden prompt set and an additional holdout. if we see drift we fall back.
[07:15] Ethan: what's the expected CPU overhead of these calibration steps?
[07:19] Maya: negligible during inference; calibration is offline. runtime cost might go up 2-3% if we add extra quant-dequant for hybrid layers.
[07:29] Carlos: remind me, does Redwood support mixed-precision per-layer?
[07:33] Maya: yes — we can run mixed-precision schedules: some critical layers in FP8, others in INT8. that's how you get a good tradeoff.
[07:41] Samir: ok practical nexts: people, deliverables, and dates.
[07:46] Maya: I'll attach the kernel traces and the small script to reproduce the micro-bench.
[07:52] Samir: I'll send the cost model and the security excerpts.
[07:56] Carlos: we'll upload the prompt sets and stand up the test node.
[07:59] Priya: also can you include a recommended rollout gating table? like allowed SNR drop, p95 thresholds, max canary percent.
[08:08] Samir: yes — sample gating table: canary 5%, SNR delta <= 2%, p95 <= SLA+15% for 30m window. If breach -> automatic degrade to FP8. We'll put that in the playbook doc.
[08:22] Ethan: ok that helps. do you have an example of a past rollout where this flow prevented production issues?
[08:28] Maya: yes — quick example: another customer started at 10% canary, we caught a 4% SNR drop in a niche extraction flow and auto-failed to FP8; fixed calibration and re-ran canary.
[08:40] Carlos: that's reassuring.

Closing and recap
[08:50] Samir: recap — action items and due dates as noted. major asks: sample prompts, infra rerun, cost model, security notes. reconvene next Tue for the readout.
[09:02] Priya: sounds good.
[09:05] Ethan: thanks everyone.
[09:07] Carlos: thanks, bye.
